entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds too much like a word from a book to hurt - its strangeness softens the greed into something funny.
examples: edacious vultures

entries.definition: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-y* ending makes the pig little - small enough to carry no real anger.
examples: the piggy fat-cheeked little boy and his porcine pot-bellied father

entries.definition: capable of being reached or attained
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same informal word written as one lump, clumsier on the page than *get-at-able* and no different in force.
examples: a very getatable man
both oil and coal are there but not in getatable locations

entries.definition: easily approached
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and literal where *approachable* is inviting: it notes the ease and adds nothing to it.

entries.definition: lacking the requisite qualities or resources to meet a task
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs what is brought against what the task needs and finds a mismatch, where *inadequate* calls the lack a fault in the thing.
examples: she was unequal to the task

entries.definition: giving an advantage
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, calculating approval: it weighs only the edge a thing gives you, not whether that edge is deserved or does any good.
examples: a contract advantageous to our country
socially advantageous to entertain often

entries.definition: manifesting partiality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Accusing where its neighbours approve - it treats favouring one side as the wrong itself, not as a favour worth having.
examples: a discriminatory tax

entries.definition: (used in combination) affected by something overwhelming
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Added to another word, its blow lands like a spell: softer-sounding than *stricken*, but just as total.
examples: conscience-smitten

entries.definition: likely to be affected by something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names exposure, not outcome: nothing has landed yet, the thing just stands open to it, unlike every struck-and-overcome word here.
examples: the bond is subject to taxation
he is subject to fits of depression

entries.definition: a mistake that results from taking one thing to be another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names how it happened - one thing taken for another - which lets the mistake sound explainable rather than someone's fault.
examples: he changed his name in order to avoid confusion with the notorious outlaw

entries.definition: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cool: it notes the reaching for recognition or advancement without judging it, where *aspiring* sounds warm.

entries.definition: full of spirit; full of life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More formal than *lively* and carrying more weight: the same fullness of life, sounding like a force inside, not liveliness on show.
examples: a vital and charismatic leader

entries.definition: expressing yourself readily, clearly, effectively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves of how the words come out - without friction - and is a plainer word than *eloquent*.

entries.definition: speaking or spoken fittingly or pleasingly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approves speech that fits the occasion or pleases the ear, where *fluent* asks only that the words come easily.
examples: a well-spoken gentleman
a few well-spoken words on civic pride

entries.definition: feeling shame or guilt or embarrassment or remorse
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for the feeling, wide enough for guilt and remorse as well as shame; unlike *disgraced*, it says nothing about reputation.
examples: are you ashamed for having lied?
felt ashamed of my torn coat

entries.definition: showing a sense of guilt
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scornful, and it paints a picture: guilt shown as a shrinking, beaten posture, and the word enjoys saying so.
examples: the hangdog and shamefaced air of the retreating enemy

entries.definition: made to feel uncomfortable because of shame or wounded pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Where *mortified* measures how sharp the discomfort is, this measures how far down it puts a person, through shame or wounded pride.
examples: humiliated that his wife had to go out to work

entries.definition: mentally perceptive and responsive
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shows a sharp, noticing mind as full of life - stirred and answering, rather than simply watchful.
examples: alive to what is going on

entries.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The *-ed* form turns it around: the thing is defined by the dread already aimed at it, where *dreadful* says it causes dread.
examples: polio is no longer the dreaded disease it once was

entries.definition: (superlative of ‘good’) having the most positive qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The highest form itself - it ends the comparison rather than making one.
examples: the best film of the year
the best solution
the best time for planting
wore his best suit

entries.definition: having or covered with or accompanied by blood
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for blood in a thing, on it, or simply alongside it, and it judges none of these.
examples: a bloody nose
your scarf is all bloody
the effects will be violent and probably bloody
a bloody fight

entries.definition: accompanied by bloodshed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts a butcher's hand on the bloodshed - crude, like a day's work, and scornful of whoever did it, where *slaughterous* is merely grand.

entries.definition: characteristic of or capable of or having a tendency toward killing another human being
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical in tone and wide in reach: it covers a settled tendency to kill, the bare ability, and what is typical of killing.
examples: a homicidal rage

entries.definition: marked by eagerness to resort to violence and bloodshed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and its cool tone sits strangely on an eagerness for bloodshed, condemning from a distance where *bloodthirsty* condemns close up.
examples: went after the collaborators with a sanguinary fury that drenched the land with blood

entries.definition: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Its *un-* means not a ripple raised, so it hints at water that held its surface, where *smooth* just describes one.
examples: unruffled water

entries.definition: without or almost without wind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare measure - no wind, or almost none - without the approval *tranquil* carries.
examples: he prefers windless days for playing golf

entries.definition: developed or executed with care and in minute detail
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The *-ed* form, cooler than *elaborate*: it marks a thing as having been worked out rather than admiring the result.
examples: the carefully elaborated theme

entries.definition: excessively or unduly careful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunter than *overcareful*: 'too' spells out the excess in plain words, where *overcareful* tucks it into the front of the word.
